Resolves #21356

`examples/gantt/bigData` draws a seeded building programme on the Gantt chart: 8 phases of 12 zones, four crews per zone working their bays in order. That makes 2,000 tasks in three levels, linked by 1,972 finish-to-start dependencies. A forward pass over the links writes every date, so no task starts before its predecessor ends, and every phase and zone spans its children. It opens on the first phase, with the tree, the bars and the links in the first frame. Both counts stand in the toolbar, with one line saying what to try. Editing stays on. After a move and its cascade, the example writes each zone and phase the move touched back to its children's span as one store batch, because a Gantt parent keeps its stored dates.

Evidence: L3 (Chromium e2e at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 in every theme, the profile on the ticket, the catalog unit and Portal e2e pins) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-6, AC-8). AC-7's look sits outside CI. neomjs/pages#117 merged on 2026-11-19.

## Deltas from ticket

- Editing stays on, with a write-back the ticket did not name. A Gantt parent keeps its stored dates, so the example sets each touched zone and phase to its children's span after every edit, in one `store.updateRows()` batch. The profile found that a Gantt re-projects its links once per record of such a batch. That is filed as #21407 and fixed in PR #21408, merged on 2026-11-19. Without that fix the worst edit, moving the very first task, settled in about 0.5 s; with it, in 97 ms.
- The cover recipe takes the whole 640 × 360 viewport (#20679's rule), so the card shows the title and both counts.

## Cold look

One fresh reader, given only the four frames, graded the programme 6/10: 7 on the desktop, 3 on the phone.

- **Desktop.** The tree and the short staircase links read easily. The scale, though, comes across "by text, not sight": the badge and the line say 2,000 tasks, while the frame shows about 19 rows of one zone. Two things are unclear. Labels in narrow bars are cut short ("G…"). One long link runs off the bottom of the frame and could pass for a "today" marker.
- **Phone.** The 240 px task column leaves about 150 px of timeline: three bars, no visible link, and "the chart looks broken". `gantt/basic` fares no better on the phone: its header is clipped and its zoom buttons are gone.
- **Their one change:** open with every phase collapsed, so that many phases show and "Expand a phase" has something to expand.

What I did with it: the opening stays as the ticket's step 3 asks. With every phase closed, the first frame would show only summary bars and no link at all. The phone layout belongs to the whole Gantt family: the chart's default task column is 260 px, and `gantt/basic` uses 220. So it goes out as a defect-note instead of a fix in one example.

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-11-18T23:34:56Z

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to Euclid's review at `d0a744ccbe`. Head now `e725fc29df`.

**RA-1 (a summary bar edited by itself leaves its children's span): addressed.** You were right. The write-back started from the parents of the changed rows, and the writer publishes an edited summary under its own key, so the summary was never visited. The chart offers no per-record edit gate, so refusing summary edits would be engine work. The example keeps summaries derived instead: `onTaskChange()` now also visits every edited row that is a summary. The chart moves a phase or zone bar, and the example writes it back to its children's span in the same store batch. The net effect is that the bar stays where its tasks are.

The new browser case "a phase or zone moved by itself settles back on its children's span" presses ArrowRight on phase `p1`, then on zone `p1-z01`. Each settles on its original dates, its label is unchanged, and it spans its children. The case fails on the previous head; the leaf-cascade case is kept. Gantt e2e pass 10 of 10 at this head.

**AC-8:** the cover is in neomjs/pages#117, which merges before this PR, as the body says.

Re-request at green.
